source.title_on_document: CommSketch: How Speaking while Sketching Steers Human–AI Design Ideation

supplement.holds: No supplement or online appendix is mentioned. Appendix A (interaction coding codebooks, Tables 6-8) is inside this PDF, pp. 17-19.

paper_design_summary: 24 participants with design coursework or practice were randomly assigned to one of two versions of the same AI sketch-to-chatbot prototype (12 per arm) and freely ideated toaster designs for 30 minutes. In Sketch-Only the AI (Gemini 2.5 Flash) interpreted the sketch alone; in CommSketch it interpreted the sketch plus a transcript of the participant's concurrent speech. Outcomes are post-task self-reported Creativity Support Index items and human-AI collaboration items, plus qualitative coding of design intent, follow-up actions, and creative agency patterns; no creativity or diversity score is computed on the designs.

studies.label: Between-subjects user study (toaster design ideation, Sketch-Only vs CommSketch)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Interface condition: AI interprets the sketch alone (Sketch-Only) or the sketch plus the concurrent speech transcript (CommSketch); both arms use generative AI
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to Sketch-Only (n = 12) or CommSketch (n = 12).

arms.name: Sketch-Only
arms.description: Participants sketch on an iPad canvas; opening the chatbot triggers an AI interpretation of the sketch alone; text and image generation available

arms.name: CommSketch
arms.description: Same prototype, task, and AI pipeline; speech is recorded and transcribed while sketching and the transcript is added to the sketch as context for the AI interpretation

participants.exclusions: None stated; Tables 4 and 5 report n = 12 per condition.
participants.who: Participants with prior design-ideation experience through university coursework or professional practice; mostly architecture, engineering-design, and other undergraduates, plus master's/PhD students and a few practitioners (automotive designer, UI designer)
participants.country: Singapore (author affiliation, Singapore University of Technology and Design); participant country not stated
participants.quote: We recruited 24 participants with prior experience in design ideation through university coursework or professional practice (Table 1).

ai_tool.name_model: gemini-2.5-flash for interpretation; Gemini 2.5 Flash (text) and Gemini 2.5 Flash Image (image generation)
ai_tool.how_used: A chatbot beside the sketch canvas gives an AI interpretation of the current sketch (plus speech transcript in CommSketch), then accepts text prompts and generates text and images that can be imported onto the canvas. Image generation was 77.4 percent (Sketch-Only) and 86.3 percent (CommSketch) of AI-use events (p. 10, Section 4.1.3).

task.description: "freely ideate toaster designs within 30 minutes" on an iPad canvas with Apple Pencil, individually

outcomes.name: Perceived alignment (human-AI collaboration questionnaire item)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Seven-point Likert item adapted from prior work [28, 30]; two-sided Mann-Whitney U, rank-biserial correlation, Holm correction across 7 collaboration items

contrasts.reported: Alignment: Sketch-Only Md 3.5 [3.00, 5.00] vs CommSketch Md 6.0 [5.75, 7.00]; U = 22.5, δ = 0.69, p_raw = .004, p_Holm = .028 (n = 12 per condition)

outcomes.name: Perceived expressiveness (Creativity Support Index item)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Seven-point Likert item adapted from the Creativity Support Index; six CSI items reported (exploration, inspiration, immersion, expressiveness, enjoyment, results worth effort); none significant after Holm correction

contrasts.reported: Expressiveness: Sketch-Only Md 4.5 [4.00, 5.00] vs CommSketch Md 6.0 [5.00, 7.00]; U = 32.0, δ = 0.56, p_raw = .019, p_Holm = .097 (n = 12 per condition)

outcomes.name: Participants expressing experience-related design intent (Design Intent coding)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Hand coding (two coders, Cohen's κ = .79) of sketches, annotations, and, in CommSketch, concurrent speech into Form, Function, Experience; participant counted once per category. Describes intent expressed, not creativity of the design.

contrasts.reported: Experience-related intentions: 9 of 12 CommSketch vs 2 of 12 Sketch-Only participants; Function 12 vs 10; Form 12 vs 12; no test reported

eligibility.reason: Randomized lab experiment comparing two AI configurations (sketch-only vs sketch plus speech context), but only 24 people were randomized and analyzed (12 per arm; p. 5, Section 3.4), well below 50. Outcomes are also self-reported creativity-support and collaboration ratings plus qualitative process coding; no creativity or diversity score is computed on the designs. Listed in the screening report as a small randomized experiment.

one_line_finding: With 12 participants per arm, adding concurrent speech to the AI's sketch context raised self-reported alignment (median 6.0 vs 3.5; U = 22.5, δ = 0.69, p_Holm = .028; p. 11, Table 5), while no Creativity Support Index item survived Holm correction (p. 9, Table 4).
notes: paper_primary for S1-O1 and S1-O2 refers to the central questionnaire outcome families; no individual item is designated primary (p. 8, Section 4). standardized_effect denotes the reported rank-biserial correlation, not a standardized mean difference (p. 6, Section 3.6.1). S1-O3 reports descriptive participant counts in both the text and Figure 5; no means, SDs, inferential test, or uncertainty are provided. statistics_available = none indicates that none of the listed categories accurately describes these counts, which remain in reported (p. 8, Section 4.1.1; p. 9, Figure 5). Eligibility was re-evaluated and remains core no, context_class none: creativity support is self-reported (p. 6, Section 3.6.1), and evaluating the creativity of resulting designs is proposed as future work (p. 14, Section 5.3).

rejected.why: Partially rejected: the counts are not figure-only, and that error is corrected. However, the proposed arm_means_sds_ns label would imply means and SDs that are not reported. The paper gives descriptive category counts and group denominators, with no inferential test or uncertainty. Used none to indicate that none of the listed statistical summary types fits, explained this in notes, and retained all printed counts in reported.
